title: TAP Role Definitions
description: Schema for tap_auth/roles.json — named capability bundles granted to protected groups. A mandatory top-level description states what/why; each role declares a mandatory description and either an explicit capability list or "*" (admin-only wildcard). Semantic checks the schema cannot express — wildcard is admin-only, every named capability is defined, the bootloader role excludes grid.purge/grid.delete — are enforced by the loader (tap_auth/roles.py) and guard tests. See spec-tap-auth-v0 req-tap-auth-roles.

description.description: What this file is and why it exists (mandatory).

roles.description: Role key -> role definition. Keys are the protected group/actor built-in keys (e.g. 'tap_admin', 'tap_cares.collector').

description.description: What the role is for and why it holds the capabilities it does (mandatory).

description_json.description: Optional structured context, flowed to ProtectedGroup.description_json (queryable alongside the prose description for AI/security reasoning).

assignable_to.description: The principal classes this role may be granted to (mandatory, non-empty). 'human' = grantable to a person via the deploy profile's auth.initial_grants login path; 'program' = bindable to a built-in program actor in sync.py. A role may declare both (tap_admin). The security boundary made explicit: a human-only role is never a program actor's bundle, and a program-only role (tap_bootloader, tap_cares.*) can never be handed to a person by login config. The loader exposes the 'human' set as LOGIN_GRANTABLE_ROLES; the auth-boot-section initial_grants enum is held in sync with it, and program bindings are checked against the 'program' set, by guard tests (req-tap-auth-roles).

capabilities.description: Either '*' (every defined capability — admin-only, enforced by the loader) or an explicit list of capability names.
